_comment: Pterodactyl egg for Bedrokia - Minecraft: Bedrock Edition server written in C# (https://github.com/Nexiumpvp2/bedrokia)
name: Bedrokia
author: nexiumpvp2@users.noreply.github.com
description: Bedrokia: a Minecraft Bedrock Edition server engine written in C# / .NET 10, mostly by AI. Supports plugins (C# source, no compilation needed), resource packs and imported Bedrock worlds. Players join through NetherNet (WebRTC), every one on the server's main port (TCP + UDP): no extra allocation needed.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Bedrokia install script: downloads the Linux server from the GitHub releases.
# The installer image already has curl; apt only runs when it is missing (apt can hang without DNS).
command -v curl >/dev/null || { apt update && apt install -y curl ca-certificates; }

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

REPO="Nexiumpvp2/bedrokia"
if [ -z "${VERSION}" ] || [ "${VERSION}" == "latest" ]; then
    URL="https://github.com/${REPO}/releases/latest/download/bedrokia"
else
    URL="https://github.com/${REPO}/releases/download/${VERSION}/bedrokia"
fi

echo "Downloading ${URL}"
curl -fsSL -o bedrokia "${URL}" || { echo "Download failed"; exit 1; }
chmod +x bedrokia

# The panel fills these keys at each start; the server adds the other ones with comments.
if [ ! -f server.properties ]; then
    printf 'server-port=%s
max-players=%s
motd=%s
webrtc-ports=%s
' "${SERVER_PORT}" "${MAX_PLAYERS}" "${MOTD}" "${WEBRTC_PORTS}" > server.properties
fi
mkdir -p plugins plugin_data resource_packs worlds players
echo "Bedrokia installed."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: Release to install: latest, or a tag such as v0.3.0.

variables.name: Server name (MOTD)
variables.description: Name shown in the server list.

variables.name: Game mode
variables.description: survival, creative or adventure (for new players).

variables.name: Xbox Live authentication
variables.description: on: players are verified with Xbox Live. off: anyone can join under any name.

variables.name: WebRTC UDP ports
variables.description: auto = every player on the main port (TCP + UDP). Or a range like 25600-25630 to give each player a port of its own (all of them must then be allocations of this server).
